To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

autoantibodies against gangliosides and the synaptic vesicle protein, SNAP‐25, bind to their respective targets on the pre‐synapse and induce neurotoxic effects, which may be attenuated by antibody uptake.
autoantibody uptake into the pre‐synapse is a key mechanism of neurotoxicity and that this uptake can be modulated by the presence of autoantibodies to intracellular targets.
the pre‐synaptically located gangliosides GM1 and GD1a act as binding sites for potentially neurotoxically active autoantibodies in patients with autoimmune neuropathies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the pre‐ synapse as a site for autoantibody‐mediated neuroinjury in autoimmune motor neuropathis and synaptopathic disorders.
understanding the mechanisms by which antibodies can enter the motor nerve terminal and cause disease, and how the pre‐synapse is a potential target of autoimmunity.
understanding the mechanisms of antibody‐induced neurotoxicity and the role of the pre‐ synaptically localized gangliosides as targets for these potentially neurotoxic antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pre‐synptic nerve terminal represents a site for antibody uptake and neurotoxicity, which is a key pathogenic mechanism in human autoimmune neuropathies.

the pre‐synaptosome is a key site for the pathogenic action of autoantibodies in autoimmune motor neuropathic disorders and that these antibodies are a major cause of the motor nerve injury in these diseases.

autoantibody binding to the pre‐synaptically expressed gangliosides is a critical event in the pathogenesis of a range of autoimmune neuropathies, including Guillain‐Barre syndrome, multifocal motor neuropathy, Miller Fisher syndrome and acute motor axonal neuropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

autoantibody‐mediated neurotrophin uptake is a novel mechanism for the induction of autoimmune neuropathy, and that the nerve terminal acts as a site for both neurotoxicity and neuroprotection in autoimmune neuropathic disease.
the pre‐synapse is an important site of autoantibody‐mediated neurodegeneration in autoimmune motor neuropathic and synaptopathic conditions.
the gangliosa‐rich pre‐snaptic motor nerve terminal acts as an autoantigenic target and a site for autoantibody uptake in autoimmune motor nerve diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre‐synapse is not just a target for neurotoxic autoantibodies but is also a site where the antibody can be taken up into the intracellular environment.
autoantibodies can act as a Trojan horse for the transfer of neurotoxicity from the nerve terminal to the cell body of motor neurons, where they can cause cell death.
autoantibodies can act as both local neurotoxins and systemic neurotrophins, and that their pathological effects can be modulated by the balance between these two activities.
